I get that most of Starfleet's objectives are exploratory and diplomatic in nature, but they still run into hostile forces from time to time. It seems to me like at least having a few fighters on a ship to fly escort when necessary would be a good plan, so why are fighters not used?
[Star Trek] Why were starfighters not widely used?
Seriously. The dinky little shuttles were completely useless. Even during normal, non-combat missions.

It would have a fraction of the energy available for weapons and shields. It's questionable that it would even be able to penetrate the shields of a typical Star Trek ship, and a fighter would be extremely vulnerable to capital ship-sized weapons, which are shown to be highly accurate and able to fire in any direction.

I'm not even sure that dogfighting in space is practical. When ever you wanted to change direction, you would have to accelerate to overcome your momentum. If nothing else, it would burn a lot of fuel.

The short answer is phasers are op.

The longer answer is that federation tech is baller. Its never quite shown on screen just how immensely powerful these starships armaments really are. They are the culmination of many, many species co-operation (see: The Federation) and the work shows.

Canonically, the Enterprise D could lay waste to cities, or even large sections of planets from orbit. These aren't just lasers remember, those are worthless in comparison. Literally cannot penetrate the navigation shield used to move stellar dust particles out of the way.

The reason a lot of people think they might be viable is the apparent charge time of a phaser discharge shown throughout the show, but the reason for that lead time is because of the immense power required for starship to starship combat. Its been shown just how fast phaser banks can fire when they dont require full power, the answer is very fast and still immensely powerfully.

The best answer of all, is demonstration, I think. THIS is why

There is also a secondary reason that smaller ships are not viable in the star trek universe. This again, did not quite come across properly on-screen.

The federation is VAST. Travel time for trips, even at high warp, are often months long. This is the true reason for the immense size of federation ships, and why families were aboard the next generation of pioneering vessels like the Enterprise D. You dont just jump to the next star, you have to pack.

Smaller shuttles or fighters would HAVE to be carried, even some of the most advanced shuttles the federation had by late TNG era movies could only manage warp 2-3. Thats fantastically slow, so slow in fact that it doesnt really make sense to have installed warp engines in them.

You couldn't actually GO anywhere with them. Maybe within half a system or something it would make sense, but your not getting to the next star any-time soon.

So fighters, then, unable to really go anywhere meaningful cant fly combat air patrols, cant be attached to a fleet and can be shot down like they were never there, and are unlikely to be able to carry enough firepower to actually make any kind of impact on capital vessels anyway.

Basically, Trek star-ships are the wooden galleys of space, and anything smaller are the longboats of space. Small, pathetically short range and cant hold a cannon.

I like to equate Star Fleet with the US Navy as opposed to the USAF. It's ship to ship warfare, and resources are better used by beefing up the bigger ships than having smaller, less capable ones flying around. It's the same reason the US doesn't have any blue water "fighter" ships.

Although technology changes tactics on a regular basis, it's hard to imagine fighters ever actually being useful in space combat. Even Earthly air combat in thirty years is likely to look like a couple of giant "mothership" planes launching giant fleets of drones against one another.

Back to space though, two capital ships face off. Either they do this at a ridiculously vast distance, or they have sufficient stealth technology to allow one to sneak up on the other undetected. Either way, they now attempt to hurl vast amounts of energy at one another while dodging whatever the other ship is throwing. Assuming they have directed-energy weapons which move at the speed of light, dodging is out of the question, so depending on available technology you either sit there trying to deflect/dump it or you fucking blow up.

So, victory either goes to whoever shoots first (gunslinger style) or whoever can hit harder and absorb more damage (sumo style).

What role do fast, maneuvrable but poorly-armed and shielded fighters have in this? Sod all -- they will be blasted to hell the moment they are detected. Hitting a moving object in space with a directed energy weapon is trivially easy.

There are certainly ways that fighters could be used even in capital ship-based space combat. Just off the top of my head they could flank around the back to either force the capital ship to pull power away from forward deflectors into the back or attack an unshielded section while the capital ship pounds on the shields themselves. They could also get in close enough to drop bombs or be used as boarding vehicles. Also, not every battle's focus is the total destruction of the enemy. If the opposing capital ship is simply acting as defense for a more vulnerable target, the friendly capital ship could engage it while the fighters weave their way through the battle and take out the main objective.
